# `missingConcurrencyOption`

Reports Effect.all and Effect.forEach calls without an explicit concurrency option, which run sequentially by default

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Style |
| Default severity | `off` |
| Fixable | Yes |
| Effect versions | v3, v4 |
| Diagnostic codes | `TS377188` |
| Language Service name | `missingConcurrencyOption` |
| Oxlint name | `effecttsgo/missing-concurrency-option` |

## Preview

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect"

declare const items: ReadonlyArray<number>
declare const save: (n: number) => Effect.Effect<void>

export const program = Effect.forEach(items, save)
/**
                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ effecttsgo(missing-concurrency-option): `Effect.forEach` runs sequentially unless `concurrency` is set; pass `{ concurrency: 1 }` to keep sequential execution or set the concurrency you intend.
*/
```

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/@effect/tsgo/schema.json",
  "compilerOptions": {

        "name": "@effect/language-service",
        "diagnosticSeverity": {
          "missingConcurrencyOption": "warning"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
